title: The Lindy Effect: Skills That Outlast Every AI Tool
alt_title_1: Stop Chasing 6-Month Tech Trends (Use the Lindy Filter)
alt_title_2: The 2,000-Year Rule for Choosing Future-Proof Skills
description_hook: Software tools change every couple of years, while some human skills have been valued for centuries. Here is how the Lindy Effect, formalized by Benoit Mandelbrot and popularized by Nassim Taleb, points to 4 skills to build alongside AI.

scenes.headline: Why So Many Tech Tutorials Expire Fast
scenes.stat_label: TYPICAL HALF-LIFE OF TRENDY SOFTWARE TACTICS
bullets: App interfaces and prompt tricks change constantly
Some old human skills keep their value for centuries
scenes.narration: Many of the software tutorials trending this month will be out of date within a couple of years, yet some very old human skills keep getting more valuable.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)

scenes.headline: Mandelbrot & Taleb's Lindy Effect
scenes.stat_label: PROVEN LIFESPAN OF TIMELESS HUMAN FOUNDATIONS
bullets: Non-perishable ideas age in reverse: survival predicts longevity
Every century a skill endures proves permanent demand
scenes.narration: Mathematician Benoit Mandelbrot formalized it and author Nassim Taleb popularized it as the Lindy Effect: for non-perishable things like ideas and skills, the longer something has lasted, the longer it is likely to last.
scenes.source: Nassim Nicholas Taleb, Antifragile (2012), the Lindy Effect

scenes.headline: Expiring Tactics vs Compounding Foundations
scenes.left_body: Memorizing app buttons and fleeting platform hacks
scenes.right_body: Clear writing, persuasion, systems design, capital allocation
scenes.narration: Chasing shiny app workflows puts you on a treadmill that resets every two years. Mastering clear writing, behavioral persuasion, systems design, and capital allocation compounds for life.

scenes.headline: The 80/20 Lindy Learning Portfolio
scenes.stat_subtext: 80% permanent foundations • 20% modern AI execution tools
scenes.narration: Use the eighty-twenty Lindy rule: spend twenty percent of your learning budget on modern AI tools, and eighty percent sharpening timeless two-thousand-year-old foundations.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)

scenes.headline: Amplify What Never Goes Out of Style
scenes.stat_label: BUILD ON BEDROCK, AUTOMATE THE REST
bullets: Tools change every season; human psychology stays constant
Own the judgment layer software cannot commoditize
scenes.narration: Treat new software as a power amplifier on top of permanent human judgment, because in an AI-accelerated economy you have to remember that...
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
